replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form (ax² + bx + c = 0). Then calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real roots; zero, one real root; negative, two complex roots. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / (2a). This method works reliably for all cases.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f’(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Plug them back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. Check if they’re maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
